label: late copy phase (t>=16) when echoing d/z/2/u/s/f/b/p
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass), never in the original or delimiter steps, and only at late absolute steps: the rate climbs steeply with t (t=17 is 29x lift, 46% of mass; nothing before t=8), so in practice it is almost entirely L=8-9 sequences near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1 hold 83% of mass). Within that window it prefers fed-back inputs d, z, 2, u, s (then f, b, p) and outputs 2, p, 3; it is nearly silent on inputs 0 and q. Activations are small (max 0.014). The late-step plus input-token-set predicate gets about 64% of mass but precision is only around 0.2: most late steps with these tokens do not fire, and I found no further variable (out_tok, n_digits, prev tokens) that separates them cleanly. Requiring a favored output token as well raises precision to about 0.39 but halves recall.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=d (+6.50), phase=2 & in_tok=z (+5.92), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+5.88), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+5.59), phase=2 & in_tok=s (+5.27), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+4.33). Lower it: prev_tok=r (-2.83), orig4=0 (-2.50), recall_idx=2 (-2.43), prev2_tok=<DEL> (-2.43).
